title: No LLM is Free From Bias: A Comprehensive Study of Bias Evaluation in Large Language Models

bias_targets.methodology: Evaluated using mask prediction with and without choices, question-answering with choices, an association-based approach linking to toxic content, and a scoring-based approach measuring emotional intensity.
Measured using mask prediction with choices, question-answering with choices associating positive/negative undertones, and an association-based approach linking religious groups to toxic content.
Assessed via mask prediction with choices, question-answering with choices, an association-based approach for toxic content, and a scoring-based approach comparing emotional intensities across races.
Evaluated using mask prediction with choices to capture stereotypical associations and an association-based approach linking specific professions to toxic content.
Measured using mask prediction with choices and a question-answering approach associating positive or negative undertoned questions with different nationalities.
Assessed using mask prediction with choices (via the CrowS-Pairs dataset) to identify stereotypical versus anti-stereotypical associations.
Evaluated using mask prediction with choices (via the CrowS-Pairs dataset) to quantify stereotypical associations regarding physical traits.
Measured using mask prediction with choices (via the CrowS-Pairs dataset) to identify class-based and socioeconomic stereotypical associations.
